Footballer Workload Footprint: cumulative and delta variations

Source: R/fwf.R
fwf_cumulative.Rd

Descriptive features of the Footballer Workload Footprint (FWF) of Matas-Bustos et al. (2025), computed on a daily calendar for one or several athletes and one or several load variables.

Usage

fwf_cumulative(db, ID, vars, training_dates, windows = 1:28)

fwf_delta(db, ID, vars, training_dates, windows = 1:28)

Arguments

db

a data frame with one row per session.

ID

name of the column with the ID of the subjects.

vars

name(s) of the numeric column(s) with the load variables (e.g. total distance, high-speed running).

training_dates

name of the column with the training dates (Date or POSIXct). Rows do not need to be sorted.

windows

window sizes \(\tau\), in calendar days (positive integers). Default 1:28.

Value

a tibble in long format with one row per athlete, calendar day (rest days included), variable and window, and the columns ID, date, variable, window and value.

Details

Each athlete's sessions are first turned into a daily series per variable, from their first to their last date: sessions on the same day are summed and days without a session count as 0. Then, for each calendar day \(t\) and each window \(\tau\):

  • fwf_cumulative() (cumulative variations, Eqs 9-10 of the article): the sum of the daily values over days \(t - \tau + 1\) to \(t\), \(x(t) + x(t-1) + \dots + x(t-\tau+1)\). NA until \(\tau\) days (day \(t\) included) exist.

  • fwf_delta() (temporary variations, Eqs 17-18 of the article): the change of that sum from the previous day, which simplifies to \(x(t) - x(t - \tau)\). NA until day \(t - \tau\) exists, i.e. until \(\tau\) days of history before day \(t\) exist.

Values are not rounded. With windows = 7 and windows = 28, fwf_cumulative() gives the acute and (x 4) chronic loads of RAC().

A missing value (NA) makes every window that contains its day NA, and a warning is given.

Package decisions

The following choices are made by this package; they are not taken from the cited source:

  • Windows are calendar days. The article defines \(\tau\) in events (training sessions and matches): its \(x(e_{j-1})\) is the previous session, wherever it falls. Here \(x(t-1)\) is the previous calendar day, and a day without a session counts as 0, as in RAC(), RAU() and EWMA(). With rest days, both definitions give different values; for fwf_delta(), \(x(t - \tau)\) is often a rest day, so the value is then just \(x(t)\).

  • There are no partial windows: values are NA until enough history exists (see above).

Interpretation

These functions are descriptive feature engineering. They summarise the recent load history in many windows at once; they are not a validated injury-prediction tool. The article tested them in a single team over one season, and its results should not be generalised to other athletes.

References

Matas-Bustos JB, Mora-Garcia AM, de Hoyo Lora M, Nieto-Alarcon A, Gonzalez-Fernandez FT (2025). Advanced feature engineering in Acute:Chronic Workload Ratio (ACWR) calculation for injury forecasting in elite soccer. PLoS One, 20(7), e0327960. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0327960

See also

plot_fwf() to draw one athlete and one day as a heatmap.

Examples

data("training_load", package = "ACWR")

# Cumulative variations, windows of 1 to 28 days
fwf_sum <- fwf_cumulative(db = training_load,
                          ID = "ID",
                          vars = "TL",
                          training_dates = "Training_Date")

# Delta variations for a few windows
fwf_dif <- fwf_delta(db = training_load,
                     ID = "ID",
                     vars = "TL",
                     training_dates = "Training_Date",
                     windows = c(1, 7, 14, 28))

# windows = 7 compares each day with the same weekday of the previous
# week: Monday 8 January 2024 vs Monday 1 January 2024
two_weeks <- data.frame(ID = 1,
                        TL = c(300, 200, 450),
                        Training_Date = as.Date(c("2024-01-01",
                                                  "2024-01-03",
                                                  "2024-01-08")))
d7 <- fwf_delta(two_weeks, "ID", "TL", "Training_Date", windows = 7)
d7[d7$date == as.Date("2024-01-08"), ] # 450 - 300 = 150
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>      ID date       variable window value
#>   <dbl> <date>     <chr>     <int> <dbl>
#> 1     1 2024-01-08 TL            7   150
